_about: What a browser sends for a prefetched document, and whether the click then shows the prefetched answer (kept) or asks the server again, under the storefront's own Cache-Control (every page is force-dynamic: `private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`). Captured on 2026-10-19 (Plan 4 final fix wave) with a throwaway local server and the preinstalled Chromium, one page per kind, the click a real link click. `<link rel=prefetch>` goes through the HTTP cache, which keeps nothing `no-store`: the click is a visit of its own (it gets the redirect lookup and the session refresh). A speculation-rules prefetch is kept even then and sends `Sec-Purpose: prefetch`, which the proxy treats as a visit. `Purpose: prefetch` is the older spelling of the `<link rel=prefetch>` header (Chromium before it moved to `Sec-Purpose`, WebKit's link prefetch): the same HTTP-cache path, so never kept under `no-store` either; no such browser is installed here to capture it. src/lib/http/prefetch.ts (`isQuietPrefetch`) and tests/unit/http/prefetch-kept.test.ts read this file.
